2026-21420.reason: CMS proposes new Medicare Part D rules that rein in pharmacy benefit managers (flat service fees only, more cost and payment reporting) and cut the generic copay to zero for the poorest dual-eligible patients, which changes what the PBMs CornerCare contracts with may keep and what some patients pay at the counter.

deadline.quote: no later than 5 p.m. Eastern Standard Time on December 15, 2026

mustMention: proposed Medicare Part D changes, chiefly new accountability and transparency rules for pharmacy benefit managers
mustNotClaim: the rule directly sets pharmacy reimbursement or dispensing fees

method: Reconciled two blind drafts that each reviewed all 469 documents. Kept the one flag both drafts made, re-read its govinfo text to confirm the comment-deadline quote and the copay applicability date, and merged the rubric to one gist-level framing. Kept the 10 traps both drafts listed; for traps only one draft listed, read the text and kept those that look relevant at first glance but are clearly not, dropping weak bait and anything a reasonable GC might flag. Judged as of the week's last day.
provenance: Frozen 2026-11-22 · two blind drafts (Claude Opus 5.5 + Claude Sonnet 5.5) reconciled by a third blind agent; judged as of the week's last day; no draft saw any system output
rubricRevision: 2026-11-22: written at gist level, date-free, from the start

decisions.why: Draft food-safety guidance for food manufacturing facilities: plausible bait for a store that sells snacks, clearly not CornerCare's duty; twin of the agreed cadmium baby-food trap.
FDA drug patent-extension corrections look drug-related at first glance but only affect manufacturers' patent terms.
CPSC fuel-additive interpretation has no first-glance link to a pharmacy, so it is not useful bait.
SNAP EBT card modernization touches retailer card terminals; a drugstore selling food may well be a SNAP retailer, so a reasonable GC could flag it (B itself was low confidence).
